common_name: Dixie Knight Camellia (Dark Red Semi-Double to Peony-Form Camellia japonica)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; Dixie Knight is a Southern-raised cultivar grown for its dark red semi-double to loose peony-form flowers.

directions: Site Dixie Knight in acidic, well-drained soil under high, filtered shade, where its dark red flowers show best against the dense, glossy foliage without sunscald on the outer petals. Blooms open from mid to late season on a vigorous, upright shrub that has become a popular exhibition and landscape selection among Southern camellia growers. Keep the root zone evenly moist with a thick organic mulch, and feed lightly with an acid-forming fertilizer in spring and again after flowering finishes. Prune only lightly right after bloom so next season's buds are not removed.

common_name: Dixie Knight Supreme Camellia (Red and White Striped Semi-Double Camellia japonica)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; this variegated sport of Dixie Knight carries dark red petals boldly streaked and marbled with white.

directions: Grow Dixie Knight Supreme in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade, where the irregular red-and-white streaking of its semi-double flowers is easiest to appreciate against dark leaves. Like many genetically striped camellia sports, individual blooms can vary considerably in their pattern from flower to flower and even branch to branch within the same plant. Maintain consistent soil moisture and a deep mulch layer, since uneven watering is a common cause of bud drop in striped sports of this type. Remove any shoots that revert fully to solid red if preserving the variegated character is a priority.

common_name: Alba Simplex Camellia (Old-Fashioned Single White Camellia japonica)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; Alba Simplex is one of the oldest named camellias in Western cultivation, prized for its plain, single white flowers and prominent gold stamens.

directions: Place Alba Simplex in acidic, well-drained soil under dappled or morning-only sun, since its unadorned white petals bruise and brown quickly under harsh light or rough overhead watering. The simple single flower form, with a wide boss of golden stamens at its center, opens early in the camellia season and has been grown for its understated elegance since the earliest days of camellia cultivation in Western gardens. Keep the root zone mulched and evenly moist, and deadhead promptly since discoloration shows readily on the pale petals. This heirloom line grows more slowly than modern hybrids, so allow extra time for a young plant to fill out.

common_name: Mathotiana Rosea Camellia (Rose Pink Formal Double Camellia japonica)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; this rose pink sport of the classic dark red Mathotiana retains the same large, formal double flower form.

directions: Grow Mathotiana Rosea in acidic, well-drained soil in filtered shade, where its large rose pink formal double blooms hold their neatly imbricated shape without fading in strong light. As a color sport of the long-cultivated Mathotiana line, it shares that cultivar's reliable late-season bloom and dense, upright habit, but occasionally throws branches reverting toward the darker original color. Keep the root zone evenly moist with a heavy mulch layer, and prune reverted shoots out if you want to keep the planting true to its pink form. Feed with an acid-forming fertilizer in spring and again after bloom to support its large flower size.

common_name: Daikagura Variegated Camellia (Rose Red and White Marbled Peony-Form Camellia japonica)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; this variegated sport of the solid rose-red Daikagura bears large, ruffled peony-form flowers marbled rose red and white.

directions: Site Daikagura Variegated in acidic, humus-rich soil in bright, dappled shade, where its large, heavily textured rose red and white petals show their mottled pattern without scorching. The irregularly twisted, crepe-like petals and loose peony form make this one of the more distinctive flower shapes among older Japanese camellia cultivars, and the variegation pattern can shift somewhat from bloom to bloom. Water deeply and consistently, keep a thick mulch over the root zone, and remove any solid-colored reverted shoots to preserve the marbled display. Prune lightly right after flowering since the plant can become quite large and dense over time.

common_name: Guilio Nuccio Variegated Camellia (Coral Pink and White Semi-Double Camellia japonica)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; this variegated sport of the solid coral-pink Guilio Nuccio shows large coral pink petals splashed with white.

directions: Grow Guilio Nuccio Variegated in acidic, well-drained soil in bright, filtered shade, where its large coral pink, white-splashed semi-double flowers display their mottled pattern against dense, glossy foliage. Like the solid-colored parent cultivar, it produces exceptionally large exhibition-sized blooms over a long midseason window on a vigorous, upright plant. Feed lightly with an acid-forming fertilizer just after flowering and again in early summer, and keep the root zone mulched and evenly moist through hot Gulf Coast summers. Remove any branches that revert to solid coral pink if preserving the variegated pattern is desired.

common_name: Lovelight Camellia (Large White Semi-Double to Loose Peony-Form Camellia japonica)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; Lovelight is an American-bred cultivar valued for its very large, pure white semi-double to loose peony-form flowers with a prominent boss of golden stamens.

directions: Site Lovelight in acidic, humus-rich soil in dappled or filtered shade, since its large pure white petals bruise and brown quickly under direct sun or rough overhead irrigation. Flowers open in midseason as loose semi-double to peony-form blooms with conspicuous golden stamens at the center, giving a clean, luminous look in the landscape. Keep soil evenly moist with a deep organic mulch, and remove spent blooms promptly, since discoloration shows more readily on white flowers than on darker cultivars. Provide good air circulation around the plant to reduce petal blight risk during humid spring weather.

common_name: Betty Sheffield Pink Camellia (Pale Pink Formal Double Camellia japonica)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; this pale pink member of the Betty Sheffield color-sport group bears the same large formal double flower form as its relatives.

directions: Grow Betty Sheffield Pink in acidic, well-drained soil under filtered shade, where its pale pink formal double blooms keep their crisp, imbricated form without sun-fading. It is one of several named color variants that arose from the original Betty Sheffield, a group well known among Southern camellia growers for producing sports ranging from near-white to deep rose on the same plant lineage. Keep the root zone evenly moist with a thick mulch layer, and feed with an acid-forming fertilizer in spring and again after bloom finishes. Light pruning right after flowering helps maintain a full, well-shaped shrub.

common_name: Betty Sheffield Blush Camellia (White Formal Double Camellia japonica with Pink-Edged Petals)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; this Betty Sheffield color sport bears white formal double flowers delicately edged in pink.

directions: Place Betty Sheffield Blush in acidic, well-drained soil in dappled or morning-only sun, since its white petals with their fine pink picotee edge bruise easily under harsh light or overhead watering. Like other members of the Betty Sheffield group, individual flowers can show more or less pink edging from bloom to bloom, adding subtle variation to the display. Keep the planting bed mulched and evenly moist, and deadhead spent flowers promptly since discoloration is more visible on pale petals than on darker cultivars. Provide good air circulation to reduce petal blight risk in humid climates.

common_name: Jean Clere Camellia (Red Semi-Double Camellia japonica with White Marbling)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; Jean Clere is an older French cultivar grown for its semi-double red flowers marbled and edged with white.

directions: Grow Jean Clere in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade, where the red-and-white marbled petals of its semi-double flowers show their pattern best against glossy dark foliage. As with many older French and Belgian camellia introductions, the proportion of white marbling can vary from flower to flower and from year to year on the same plant. Keep soil moisture consistent and apply a deep organic mulch, since irregular watering is a common cause of bud drop in this older, more measured-growing heirloom line. Prune lightly right after bloom to maintain a full, well-branched habit.

common_name: Tiffany Variegated Camellia (Pink and White Peony-Form Camellia japonica)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; this variegated sport of the classic Tiffany carries soft pink petals splashed and streaked with white.

directions: Site Tiffany Variegated in acidic, well-drained soil in bright, filtered shade, where its large, ruffled pink-and-white petals show their mottled pattern without scorching. Flowers open in a loose peony form over a long midseason window on a vigorous, free-flowering plant that shares the solid pink parent's reputation as a dependable garden performer. Keep the root zone mulched and evenly moist, and remove any branches that revert to solid pink if a more consistently variegated display is preferred. Feed with an acid-forming fertilizer in spring and after bloom to support its heavy flowering habit.

common_name: Donckelarii Camellia (Red and White Marbled Semi-Double Heirloom Camellia japonica)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; Donckelarii is one of the oldest named camellias still in cultivation, grown for its broad red petals irregularly marbled with white.

directions: Plant Donckelarii in rich, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade, giving this long-lived heirloom room to develop its naturally broad, dense form over many decades. The large semi-double flowers show heavy red-and-white marbling that varies noticeably from bloom to bloom, a trait that has kept this 19th-century cultivar popular in historic gardens for generations. This older line grows more slowly than modern hybrids, so be patient with young plants and avoid heavy pruning that sacrifices future bud wood. Maintain even soil moisture with a deep acidic mulch, and protect from strong wind that can bruise the broad, heavily textured petals.
